core-ui-composed-fixture.scope: Public JSX exercises the same three fixture states through recording, packed Canvas, and React Native Web. Plain leaf opacity, isolated corner and stacking probes, and spaced Select activations have bounded host assertions. Group compositing, transparent image pixels, physical focus/repeat, typography, and device rendering need independent evidence. The Ultra 4850X on 16.0.4 build 853 rendered crop, stacking, outline and leaf opacity in a provenance-matched standalone fixture. Three corners failed natively with the nested MaskGroup implementation. The standalone target now composes one alpha bitmap for all four corners. Host tests check the alpha values and replacement/retirement; the candidate requires exact-archive stills on the Ultra.

react-native-subset.scope: React Native host subset, including committed RN/ARIA role/state/value/label semantics and English Audio Guide requests. TextInput publishes observed dialog edits, reconciles controlled formatting/rejection and fences reentrant or retired subscriptions; programmatic writes do not fabricate input changes. Observed editor selections reach onSelectionChange in UTF-16 offsets; SDK carets are collapsed and Canvas can observe ranges. Missing or retired observations do not infer a cursor; native ranges and programmatic selection remain unsupported. Keyboard.dismiss cancels the focused modal editor; keyboardDidHide requires an observed closure and follows accepted-text delivery. Missing/unshown/disposed closures do not fabricate hide, geometry or will/show events. Native accessibility traversal, speech completion/queue retirement, keyboard/focus/metrics/services require device qualification. AppRegistry registration only. Keyed vertical collections prioritize visible rows and batch offscreen additions with cancellable interaction-aware JS work; initialScrollIndex requires declared geometry and visible-position preservation respects its minimum index. Native scroll/performance remain device-pending. Authored ARIA current/invalid/popup state and explicit level/orientation/role descriptions reach committed host semantics and English focus/live requests. Native structural traversal and action delivery are not admitted by this metadata or speech profile.

flat-list-columns.scope: Vertical equal-height multi-column rows with incomplete tails and columnWrapperStyle. Original item/index delivery to renderItem and keyExtractor; original data plus row indices for declared layout, initial/index/end scrolling, batching, and separators, matching pinned React Native FlatList.js. Row keys combine item keys; changed row membership may remount items. Complete retained/visible rows, bounded large-list work, extraData, data replacement, held-input retirement and cleanup have host and independent packed-consumer evidence. Bounded SDK/Canvas fixture checks compilation, geometry, visible pixels and retirement. Horizontal grids, column-prop changes without remount and single-column columnWrapperStyle fail explicitly; masonry, native scrolling/focus/performance, full viewability remain unqualified; the separate single-callback contract is bounded.

modal-committed-back.scope: Back admission follows the top committed modal exposure instead of parent/child effect registration order. Nested removal releases the next owner, closing animations retain Back, reversals cancel retired completions, and route replacement/returns fence retired native input and portals. Focus observations and Back transport are explicit host fixtures; native remote ordering, presentation and focus restoration remain device-pending. Fully hidden siblings receive a new order when presented again, independent of component mount order; closing reversals retain their order below retained nested modals. Fixed-seed sibling schedules, independently installed public consumers and SDK/actual Canvas pixels plus preview Back-port checks establish this bounded host contract.

flat-list-horizontal.scope: Single-axis horizontal keyed windowing uses measured/declared widths, x offsets, header/footer/inset clamping, initial/index/end alignment, extraData, separators and bounded queued batches. Keyed anchors select the replacement window before reconciliation; retained owners and held input survive demonstrated insertion/reorder schedules. Independent packed consumers exercise 30,001 items with bounded mounted cells; SDK/Canvas fixture checks compilation, visible pixels, start/end geometry and retirement. Axis changes require a new React key; horizontal grids remain rejected. No native scrolling, remote focus, memory/performance or touch-drag qualification.

flat-list-separators.scope: Pinned upstream separator controller mapping: highlight/unhighlight updates current and preceding mounted row separators; leading/trailing updateProps merges custom props. Component separators receive highlighted and current leadingItem, including row arrays for grids; element separators pass through unchanged. Keyed cell state survives supported replacement, while retired or offscreen callbacks cannot target returned keys. Measured size changes retain current native items; public packed consumers and Canvas visible highlight/restoration checks pass. Native scroll/focus remain unqualified; viewability has a separate bounded contract.

image-preparation-lifetimes.scope: Resolved source/recycling-key tuples own fresh Poster readiness, dimensions and terminal state. Late observations and reentrant callback retirement cannot continue an old load or borrow a successor. Independent public Expo-alias consumers exercise partial/recycled loads and cleanup; actual browser decoding verifies same-URI recycling, failure/recovery and visible pixels. text-preparation-failure.scope: Failed renderer preparation releases ready and late sibling raster leases without publishing partial fields; committed predecessors and newer cohorts keep their ownership until replacement/unmount. Started font/raster promises remain observed after a later synchronous build/walk failure, preserving the original error and existing latched-flush contract. Public packed consumer uses the actual 80,000-byte bounded cache for failure, released-entry eviction, recovery and full retirement. Native font metrics, mask/write output and firmware timing remain device-pending. FontResources fault-port checks preserve synchronous initialization and asynchronous readiness errors, maintain the existing failed-identity budget, fence retired readiness/metrics, and retain retryable disposal authority without duplicate reentrant removal. All font cleanup is attempted before reporting its first failure; changed native source compiles through the packed SDK lane, without claiming observed firmware exception behavior. Public native-root retirement preserves the earliest render/cleanup error and attempts every remaining owner, retaining failed provider/lease cleanup for retry without replaying successful work or reviving host authority. Actual bounded cache/transport-disposal failure, service unbinding, reentrant retirement and latched-error cases have source and independent installed public-consumer evidence; native physical cleanup remains unqualified. Pinned SDK call-boundary fixtures preserve the first SDK-host shutdown failure across later errors, and keep raster dispose-request submission and owned-observer detachment independently retryable. Pending/current requests retire before cleanup, successful steps are not replayed, and the changed native source compiles from the installed archive. Native task execution and physical cleanup remain pending. Font/raster owners snapshot physical asset maps at construction, keeping prepared/in-flight native URI metadata and later-size resources consistent after caller edits or deletions. Source font checks and independent installed Node/Hermes raster-request identity checks cover this configuration boundary; measured native font fidelity remains pending. Raster reservations publish before draw/eviction callbacks, so reentrant same-key callers share one pending result within budget while distinct keys remain separately accounted. Callback retirement fences bitmap writes and prevents restored entries or negative accounting; throwing draws preserve their error. Source counterexamples and an independent installed public-cache consumer use synthetic file ports, without native file-completion claims.

collection-geometry-replay.scope: Four fixed seeds replay 64 bounded geometry/data/input actions each across one/two/three vertical columns and a horizontal lane, with minimized independent packed cases. flat-list-viewability.scope: Single callback/config profile using committed known row metrics, pinned integer-pixel/item/viewport thresholds, fully-visible admission, delayed captured-set filtering and explicit recordInteraction. native-observer-retirement.scope: Owned text-entry/device-facts observers submit the actual previous callback required by the pinned SDK unregister cue. accessibility-publication-lifetimes.scope: A synchronous announcement-port root unmount or committed replacement retires the old live-region publication before further submissions or de-duplication writes. focus-observation-lifetimes.scope: A focus observation retains its exact registered target and ordering across held-key cancellation and old-target blur. Reentrant disposal, same-ID route replacement or a newer explicit observation stops the retired continuation; removal of only the departing target preserves a live destination. back-subscription-lifetimes.scope: Back callback deduplication, LIFO priority and consumption remain preserved. Captured registrations must still own their identity at invocation; removed/replaced callbacks cannot navigate a successor, new registrations wait for the next event, and stale removal cannot delete a replacement. Gesture retirement through disposal, inactivity/reactivation or external text entry stops remaining callbacks. Actual mounted React route/provider cleanup inside an input callback has source and independent installed public-consumer evidence. This is a bounded host lifetime contract, not all upstream mutation quirks or native remote/focus timing.

application-lifetime.scope: Shared registered/custom application root, input, web/setup/content lifetime with original startup errors, async/reentrant disposal, independent cleanup and fenced retired callbacks.
